Comments:
Regional water consumption totaled approximately 84 million m³ across 19 water providers in 2022. Surface water was the dominant source of supply, accounting for approximately 50 million m³, followed by mixed-source systems (~30 million m³) and groundwater (~3 million m³). 

In 2022, the City of Kelowna was the largest municipal water consumer in the watershed, using approximately 14.3 million m³.

Two providers did not have publicly available consumption records for 2022, indicating that the reported regional total reflects the best available data but is not fully comprehensive.

Regional water consumption increased to approximately 109 million m³ across 20 providers in 2023, representing a 28.99% increase from 2022. Surface water was the dominant source of supply, accounting for approximately 55 million m³, followed by mixed-source systems (~50 million m³) and groundwater (~3 million m³). 

Greater Vernon Water was the largest municipal water provider in 2023, reporting approximately 18.5 million m³ of water consumption, followed by the City of Kelowna at approximately 15.8 million m³.

Only one provider had missing consumption data for 2023, making this year's dataset more complete than 2022.

Regional water consumption totaled approximately 108 million m³ across 19 providers in 2024, representing a 0.72% decrease from 2023. Despite the slight year-over-year decline, water demand remained high, exceeding 100 million m³ for the second consecutive year. 

Surface water was the dominant source of supply in 2024, accounting for approximately 56 million m³, followed by mixed-source systems (~47 million m³) and groundwater (~4 million m³). 

In 2024, Greater Vernon Water remained the largest municipal water provider in the watershed, reporting approximately 17.4 million m³ of consumption, followed by the City of Kelowna at approximately 15 million m³.

Two providers had missing consumption data for 2024, reducing data completeness slightly compared with 2023.

Reported water consumption for 2025 totals approximately 56 million m³ across 9 providers. However, this total reflects incomplete reporting rather than a confirmed decrease in regional water use. The reported 47.75% year-over-year decline is primarily driven by missing data, with 12 providers lacking 2025 consumption records. As a result, comparisons with previous years should be interpreted with caution. When additional 2025 consumption data becomes available, regional totals and year-over-year trends are expected to change significantly.

Among providers with available 2025 data, Black Mountain Irrigation District reported the highest water consumption at approximately 12.6 million m³, followed by the Town of Oliver at approximately 11.7 million m³.

Surface water remained the dominant reported water source, accounting for the majority of available municipal consumption data, while groundwater continued to represent the smallest share.
